newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada monthly GDP falls 0.3 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Canada monthly GDP falls 0.3 pct in March.

text.p: Canada's real gross domestic product, seasonally adjusted, fell 0.3 percent in March after rising 0.5 percent in February, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
Note: GDP figures are in billions of dollars, seasonally adjusted at annual rates at factor cost, constant 1986 dollars.
A Reuters survey of economists predicted monthly GDP would rise 0.4 percent in March after rising 0.5 percent in February.
Statistics Canada said the monthly decline in gross domestic product was due to less robust activity in manufacturing, wholesale and retail trade, areas which were strong in January and February.

Activity in forestry, transportation and storage, and community, business and personal services also eased in March, StatsCan said. Financial services also weakened, restrained for a second month in a row by a sharp drop in housing resales.
Higher production by utilities, communication services and construction moderated the overall drop, the agency said.
(For more information from Statistics Canada contact Michel Girard, Industry Measures and Analysis Division, at 613-951-9145).
